The Studio has not changed it and is not saving over it.' and offered 'Download the unreadable copy'. Work was not lost without notice. The target held.

attempts.input: Source review of every way a value could get from an input into the Mockup. preview.tsx: both iframes use sandbox="" (no allow-scripts, allow-same-origin, allow-forms or allow-top-navigation) and srcDoc. smallBusiness.ts: a CSP meta tag comes first in <head> ('default-src none; style-src unsafe-inline; img-src data:; font-src data:; form-action none; base-uri none'); every content string passes through escapeHtml (& < > " '); data-* attributes come from list-checked parameters; links are inert in previews. assertKnownParams runs before rendering. tokensToCss refuses a name outside /^--[a-z0-9-]+$/ and a value containing any of < > { } ;. Zod checks every parameter as an enum or a finite number in range. Sliders are clamped in tune(). Prefs are whitelisted. fileNameFor reduces the name to [a-z0-9-]. Downloads use application/octet-stream.
attempts.observed: I found no route that puts free text into CSS. Token values come only from numbers and list choices, and content goes only into escaped HTML text. The guard does not block backslash, quotes, parentheses or '/*' (a trailing '\' could swallow the next ';', and '/*' could comment out the rest of the stylesheet), but I found no input that can put those characters into a token value. Observation, not a break: the Studio's own page (refraction-studio.html) has no Content-Security-Policy of its own. The only CSP string in the file sits inside the bundle (byte 469806) and belongs to the Mockup template. So if a future change adds a markup sink in the Studio, nothing else stops it. Also, the probe frame in platform.ts has no sandbox, but its srcdoc is a fixed string.
